title: Preparation of chaperone-loaded neural stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles to reduce protein aggregation in Huntington's disease cellular models
protocol: Nucleofect C17.2 cells with plasmid encoding recombinant protein of interest.
Apply antibiotic pressure to select transgenic population.
Establish monoclonal stable cell line using paper disc method.
Select clone expressing high amounts of recombinant protein of interest.
Seed 2–3 × 10^6 C17.2 cells per 15 cm cell culture dish and incubate overnight at 37°C/5% CO2.
Remove the culture medium from the cells and wash with DPBS.
Incubate cells with trypsin/EDTA for 3 min or until all cells are detached.
Add complete medium to the dish, and pipette up and down to create a homogenous single-cell suspension.
Take 10 μL of the single-cell suspension and determine cell density with a hemocytometer.
Centrifuge 1 × 10^6 cells/condition at 200 g for 10 min at room temperature.
Prepare nucleofection materials by adding Supplement solution to Nucleofector™ Solution.
Start 4D-Nucleofector™ System (Lonza).
Upload DN-100 experimental parameter file for C17.2 cells.
Fill 10 mL complete culture medium in each 10 cm cell culture plate and pre-incubate plates in a humidified 37°C/5% CO2 incubator.
Pre-warm an aliquot of culture medium to 37°C.
Prepare plasmid DNA.
Centrifuge the cells for 10 min, then remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet carefully in RT 4DNucleofector™ Solution.
Add 5 μg of plasmid DNA to the cell suspension (maximum 10% of final sample volume).
Transfer the mixture to a Nucleocuvette™ Vessel.
Repeat the procedure for additional Nucleocuvette™ Vessels as required.
Tap the Nucleocuvette™ Vessels gently to cover the sample at the bottom of the cuvette.
Close the lid and place the cuvette into the retainer of the 4D-Nucleofector™ X Unit in proper orientation.
Press Start on the display of the 4D-Nucleofector™ Core Unit.
Remove the cuvette from the retainer after completing the run.
Resuspend the cells with pre-warmed medium and mix by pipetting gently only two to three times using the supplied pipettes with the kit avoiding bubble formation.
Add the cells to the cell culture plates ready for use.
Incubate the cells in humidified 37°C/5% CO2 incubator.
Wash cells with HBSS thoroughly to remove cellular debris.
Trypsinize cells and divide over 3 dishes.
Return cells to incubator for 2 days.
Incubate cells for 2 days.
Trypsinize cells with 1.5 mL trypsin/EDTA.
Resuspend cells in 10 mL complete medium.
Keep aside 2 mL of cell suspension.
Pellet down the remaining 8 mL of cell suspension at 200 g for 5 minutes.
Discard the supernatant from the pelleted cells.
Add 4 mL freezing medium (complete medium with 10% DMSO) to the pelleted cells and divide into 4 cryogenic vials.
Freeze the cells in the cryogenic vials.
Count cells in the 2 mL cell suspension set aside earlier.
Seed 50 cells in a 10 cm dish with 20 mL complete medium.
Seed 100 cells in another 10 cm dish with 20 mL complete medium.
Place both dishes in the incubator.
Check after 24 hours if cells have attached to the bottom of the dishes and look healthy.
Return the dishes to the incubator if everything is okay.
Check for colonies after 1 week post-seeding.
Ensure colonies contain at least 100 cells each and grow apart from one another.
Continue monitoring colony growth every few days.
Cut out Whatman paper (number 1) discs using a punching machine.
Autoclave the cut-out discs.
Seal the dish with parafilm.
Clean the microscope stage with 70% ethanol.
Screen the dish for colonies with GFP fluorescence.
Encircle colonies (> 12 clones) with highest fluorescence on the bottom of the dish using a marker pen.
Remove the parafilm and place the dish back in the incubator.
Warm up cell culture medium, trypsin, and HBSS.
Take 5 mL trypsin in a small dish.
Place autoclaved paper discs in the lid of the dish.
Distribute 500 μL complete medium per well in a 24-well plate.
Label the wells with numbers.
Remove the dish from the incubator and place it in the laminar flow.
Wash the dish twice with HBSS.
Flame tweezers twice and let them cool down.
Meanwhile, remove HBSS from the dish.
Dip paper discs in trypsin/EDTA and place one disc on each encircled colony.
Keep the dish in the incubator for 3 minutes.
Pick paper discs one by one and transfer to individual wells in the 24-well plate.
Pipette up and down medium in every well with a separate tip using a 1 mL micropipette.
Place the 24 well plate in the incubator.
Check the plate daily.
Discard Whatman paper discs once wells reach around 70% confluence.
Transfer cells from one well in a 24 well plate to one well in a 6 well plate.
Select clones showing maximum GFP and GFP-DNAJB6 expression at expected localizations.
Transfer each selected clone to a separate 10 cm dish.
Let cells grow until 80% confluence.
Expand each 10 cm dish to three 10 cm dishes.
Freeze cells from two dishes in five cryogenic vials.
Use the remaining 10 cm dish for downstream processing.
Dip a coverslip in 100% ethanol.
Remove excess ethanol by touching the coverslip to the beaker wall.
Flame the coverslip by holding it in the flame for a second.
Extinguish the flame by shaking the coverslip.
Place one coverslip per well.
Trpsinize wild type (WT), XP-GFP, and XP-GFP-DNAJB6b C17.2 cells.
Count the trypsinized cells.
Seed 3 × 10^4 cells in each well with coverslip in the 24-well plate.
Incubate the seeded cells for 24 hours at 37°C.
Fix cells with 4% PFA in PBS for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Wash fixed cells with PBS twice.
Permeabilize cells with 0.2% Tween-20 in PBS for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Rinse permeabilized cells with PBS.
Block cells with blocking buffer (3% BSA/PBS) for 1 hour at room temperature.
Dilute primary antibody against CD9 in blocking buffer (1:200).
Add diluted primary antibody to the cells.
Incubate cells with primary antibody overnight at 4°C.
Rinse cells with PBS thrice.
Incubate cells with secondary antibody diluted 1:500 and DAPI in blocking buffer for 30 min at room temperature.
Rinse cells with PBS.
Mount coverslips on microscope slides using Faramount mounting medium.

Investigate samples with confocal microscopy (Leica SP8, HC PL APO CS2 63×, NA 1.4, oil immersion, filter settings for DiI; excitation 551 nm, emission 565 nm and DAPI; excitation 358 nm, emission 463 nm, GFP; excitation 490 nm, emission 544 nm).
Seed 3–5 × 10^6 C17.2 sEV donor cells per flask in 10 T162 flasks with 20 mL complete medium at 37°C under 5% CO2 overnight.
Wash away the old medium with HBSS the next day and add 20 mL exosome-depleted medium to the cells.
Incubate for 48 hours, then collect approximately 180 mL of medium in 5 UC tubes (approximately 36 mL per tube).
Add an equal amount of sterile water in one UC tube for balancing purposes.
Weigh the tubes to ensure they are balanced before proceeding with centrifugation.
Remove dead cells from the supernatant by centrifuging at 500 g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Carefully transfer the supernatant to a fresh falcon tube by pipetting without touching the pellet.
Centrifuge the supernatant at 2,000 g for 10 minutes at 4°C to remove cellular debris.
Transfer the supernatants into a UC tube by pipetting without touching the pellet.
Centrifuge the resultant solution at 10,000 g for 30 minutes at 4°C to remove apoptotic vesicles and microvesicles.
Subject the supernatant to ultracentrifugation at 110,000 g for 70 minutes at 4°C to collect small extracellular vesicles (sEVs).
Resuspend the collected sEV pellet in 5 mL of cold DPBS.
Transfer the suspension into a new UC tube and perform ultracentrifugation again under the same conditions.
Re-suspend the final sEV pellet in 50 μL of cold DPBS.
Store the sEV suspension at 4°C for downstream processing.
Measure the protein concentration of sEV suspension using DC protein assay kit I.
Perform NTA analysis on diluted samples of total extracellular protein in PBS.
Dilute 1 μg and 2 μg total extracellular protein samples in 1 mL of PBS for size measurement by NanoSight LM14 with NTA software 3.0.
Measure the size of particles using NanoSight LM14 following manufacturer’s protocol.
Prepare 30 μg whole cell lysates and sEVs by mixing them with 2× Laemmli loading buffer containing SDS and protease inhibitors.
Boil samples at 90°C for 5 min before Western blot analysis.
Load boiled samples onto an SDS-PAGE gel.
Run the SDS-PAGE gel at 200 V for 2 h.
Transfer proteins from the gel to a PVDF membrane in transfer buffer at 500 mA for 1 h.
Block the membrane with Odyssey blocking buffer for 1 hour at room temperature.
Place a parafilm in a 10 cm square petri dish to match the size of the blot.
Add 300–500 μL of antibody solution prepared in Odyssey blocking buffer (1:1000) on the parafilm.
Take out the blot from the blocking solution and cut a small piece off the right corner to mark the protein side.
Place the blot with the protein side facing downward, into the antibody solution.
Place one small wet tissue paper along the edges of the petri dish without touching the blot.
Close the petri dish and incubate the blots overnight at 4°C.
Wash the blots with 0.1% PBS-Tween20 for 4 × 5 minutes.
Incubate the blots with secondary antibody solution (1:5000 in blocking buffer) for 1 hour at room temperature, following the same procedure as for primary antibody incubation.
Wash the blots with 0.1% PBS-Tween20 for 4 × 5 minutes.
Take out the blot from the petri dish.
Acquire images with an Odyssey® Infrared Imaging System following manufacturer’s protocol.
Seed Hek293T cells for the inclusion body assay on the day you prepare the western blot samples to check for DNAJB6 and EV markers.
Trypsinize Hek293T cells when their presence is confirmed.
Count trypsinized Hek293T cells.
Seed 3 × 10^4 cells in complete medium per well.
Incubate seeded cells for 24 h at 37°C.
Transfect HEK293T cells with 200 ng pEGFP-Q74 using JetPEI® for 4 hours.
Rinse the cells rigorously with HBSS to avoid cell loss.
Add 25 μg total sEV protein content to 500 μL of exosome-depleted medium (50 μg/mL per well) and add to the washed cells.
Incubate cells for 36 hours.
Take exosome-depleted medium without sEVs as control.
Fix cells with 4% PFA in PBS, pH 7.4, for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Rinse fixed cells with PBS.
Add DAPI (1 μg/mL in PBS) to the cells and incubate for 20 minutes at room temperature.
Rinse cells with PBS after adding DAPI.
Mount coverslips using Faramount mounting medium.
Image samples using fluorescence microscopy.
Set the excitation/emission settings to GFP (excitation 490 nm/emission 550 nm) and for DAPI (excitation 360 nm/emission 460 nm).
Take at least 5 images from different areas randomly for each sample.
Count the number of nuclei using ImageJ Plugins > Analyze > Cell counter.
Count the number of inclusion bodies using the same plugin.
Document all numbers in an excel file.
Get a ratio of the number of cells with inclusion bodies to the total number of transfected cells.
Repeat the experiment 3 times.
Draw a bar graph using Graphpad PRISM or any other software for analysis.
Trypsinize Hek293T cells.
Count and seed 15 x 10^4 Hek293T cells in complete medium per well.
Incubate the seeded cells for 24 hours at 37°C.
Transfect 1 μg of pEGFP-Q74 into Hek293T cells using JetPEI® according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Rinse the transfected cells rigorously with HBSS.
Add 100 μg total sEV protein content in 1 ml exosome-depleted medium (50 μg/ml per well) to the washed cells.
Incubate the cells for 36 hours.
Rinse the cells once with HBSS after incubation.
Add 400 μl of filter trap assay buffer with SDS (10 mM Tris-Cl pH 8.0, 150 mM NaCl, 2% SDS) per well to the treated cells.
Scrape the cells in each well.
Transfer the cell mass to an Eppendorf using a 1 mL tip.
Sonicate the samples.
Measure protein concentration with a DC Protein Assay Kit.
Dilute the cell lysates to achieve 1 μg/μL final concentration in assay buffer, making the total volume 285 μL per sample.
Add 15 μL of 1 M DTT to each diluted sample to make the total volume 300 μL.
Heat the samples at 95°C for 5 minutes.
Store remaining samples at -80°C for later use if necessary.
Open the Bio-Dot SF apparatus.
Clean the apparatus thoroughly with water and soap.
Prepare FTA wash buffer (10 mM Tris-Cl pH 8.0, 150 mM NaCl, 0.1% SDS).
Soak 2 thick Trans-blot papers in the wash buffer.
Place the soaked papers on the base of the Bio-Dot SF apparatus.
Soak 0.2 μm cellulose acetate membrane in buffer.
Place the membrane on trans-blot papers.
Remove air bubbles by rolling a 10 mL plastic pipette gently on the membrane.
Add the lid of the apparatus and tighten the screws diagonally.
Apply full vacuum and tighten the screws further under vacuum.
Switch off the pump, add 200 μL FTA wash buffer, and apply vacuum until all buffer goes through.
Repeat the previous step once.
Close the vacuum.
Add 100 μL of samples into each well.
Apply low vacuum very carefully to let the buffer pass through completely.
Wash the slots thrice with the given buffer.
Open the apparatus and remove the membrane.
Place the membrane in blocking buffer in a square petri dish for 1 hour at room temperature on a shaker.
Rinse the blot with PBS-T.
Add anti-GFP antibody primary antibody solution (1:2000 in Odyssey blocking buffer) to the membrane.
Incubate overnight at 4°C on a shaker.
Wash the blot with PBS-T 4 times for 10 minutes each.
Prepare the Odyssey secondary antibody mixture (1:5000 in Odyssey blocking buffer).
Incubate the blot with the mix for 1 hour at room temperature on a shaker.
Wash the blot with PBS-T 4 times for 10 minutes each.
Detect proteins on the blot with Odyssey Infrared Imaging System.
Make samples for filter trap assay from freshly made isolates.
Boil samples with loading buffer and store at -80°C until further use.
Avoid freeze-thaw cycles until sample use.
Take 30 μg of total protein from each sample.
Follow western blotting steps using anti-GFP antibody with modifications as needed.
Use the entire gel for transfer onto the PVDF membrane.
Lift and place the gel gently on the membrane during transfer.
Rearrange well walls into original position if necessary.
Draw a rectangle around bands in ImageJ of consistent size for all samples.
Measure band intensities using Analyze > Measure.
Calculate the extent of protein aggregation as a percentage with respect to control.
